items.title: Rewriting Trigonometric Ratios Using Cofunction Identities

sections.normalized_html:
First, notice that the cofunction of [MATH: \cos x] (cosine) is [MATH: \sin x] (sine). The corresponding identity is given by

[MATH: \cos x = \sin \left( \dfrac{\pi}{2} - x \right).]

Substituting [MATH: x=\dfrac{\pi}{5}] into the above, we get

[MATH: \cos((π)/(5))|= \sin((π)/(2) − (π)/(5)); = \sin ((3π)/(10)).]

Therefore, we conclude that [MATH: \cos{\left(\dfrac \pi 5\right)} = \sin\left( \dfrac {3 \pi} {10}\right).]

sections.normalized_html:
First, we recall the cofunction identity (in degrees) for sine and cosine:

[MATH: \cos x = \sin \left(30^\circ - x \right)]

Substituting [MATH: x=30^\circ - \theta] into the above, we get

[MATH: \sin(30^{∘} − θ)|= \cos(90^{∘} − (30^{∘} − θ)); = \cos ((90^{∘} − 30^{∘}) + θ); = \cos (60^{∘} + θ).]

First, we recall the cofunction identity for sine and cosine:

[MATH: \cos \left( \dfrac{\pi}{2} - y \right) = \sin y]

Substituting this into our expression, we get

[MATH: 1 − \cos((π)/(2) − y)\sin y|= 1 − \siny\sin y; = 1 − \sin^{2} y; = \cos^{2} y.]

items.title: Simplifying Expressions Using Multiple Cofunction Identities

sections.normalized_html:
First, we recall the cofunction identity for tangent and contangent:

[MATH: \tan\left(90^\circ - x \right) = \cot x]

We also recall the cofunction identity for secant and cosecant:

[MATH: \sec( 90^\circ - x ) = \csc x]

Substituting these identities into our expression and using the fact that [MATH: \cot x = \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \csc x = \dfrac{1}{\sin x},] we get the following:

[MATH: \tan(90^{∘} − x)\cos x − \sec(90^{∘} − x)|= \cotx\cos x − \cscx; = (\cosx)/(\sinx) ⋅ \cos x − (1)/(\sinx); = (\cos^{2} x − 1)/(\sin x); = (− \sin^{2} x)/(\sin x); = (− \sin x\sin x)/(\sin x); = − \sin x]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The following identities are called the cofunction identities. We can split them into three main groups.

Content:

[MATH: \sin x|= \cos ((π)/(2) − x); \cos x|= \sin ((π)/(2) − x)]
- Tangent and cotangent:
[MATH: \tan x|= \cot ((π)/(2) − x); \cot x|= \tan ((π)/(2) − x)]

Content:

---

Item 2 — Example: Rewriting Trigonometric Ratios Using Cofunction Identities

Example Prompt:
Express [MATH: \cos{\left(\dfrac \pi 5\right)}] using the corresponding cofunction.

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, notice that the cofunction of [MATH: \cos x] (cosine) is [MATH: \sin x] (sine). The corresponding identity is given by

[MATH: \cos x = \sin \left( \dfrac{\pi}{2} - x \right).]

Substituting [MATH: x=\dfrac{\pi}{5}] into the above, we get

[MATH: \cos((π)/(5))|= \sin((π)/(2) − (π)/(5)); = \sin ((3π)/(10)).]

Therefore, we conclude that [MATH: \cos{\left(\dfrac \pi 5\right)} = \sin\left( \dfrac {3 \pi} {10}\right).]

Item 11 — Example: Simplifying Expressions Using Multiple Cofunction Identities

Example Prompt:
[MATH: \tan \left( 90^\circ - x \right) \cos x- \sec\left( 90^\circ - x \right)=]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we recall the cofunction identity for tangent and contangent:

[MATH: \tan\left(90^\circ - x \right) = \cot x]

We also recall the cofunction identity for secant and cosecant:

[MATH: \sec( 90^\circ - x ) = \csc x]

Substituting these identities into our expression and using the fact that
[MATH: \cot x = \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \csc x = \dfrac{1}{\sin x},]
we get the following:

[MATH: \tan(90^{∘} − x)\cos x − \sec(90^{∘} − x)|= \cotx\cos x − \cscx; = (\cosx)/(\sinx) ⋅ \cos x − (1)/(\sinx); = (\cos^{2} x − 1)/(\sin x); = (− \sin^{2} x)/(\sin x); = (− \sin x\sin x)/(\sin x); = − \sin x]
